<section class="section wrap intro-grid">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Research perspective</p>
<h2>What can geophysical observations tell us about the subsurface?</h2>
</div>
<div>
<p>I am a Ph.D. candidate in Geophysics at Stony Brook University, working with Weisen Shen. My research seeks to understand what geophysical observations can tell us about the subsurface, from its seismic structure to its composition, temperature, porosity, and fluid conditions.</p>
<p>My research uses seismology and complementary geophysical observations to address these questions, with current work spanning the continental United States and the Antarctic interior. Polar environments are a central direction of my research.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div>
<p class="number">01 / ANTARCTIC SUBGLACIAL GEOPHYSICS</p>
<h3>A water-rich sedimentary aquifer beneath the South Pole</h3>

<p>Dense seismic observations indicate a widespread low-velocity layer beneath the
ice, interpreted as porous, water-bearing sediment. I combine seismic imaging
with rock physics and complementary radar and magnetotelluric observations to
investigate groundwater storage and hydrological conditions beneath the
Antarctic interior.
</p>
<a class="text-link" href="research.html#antarctica">
Explore Antarctic research
</a>
</div>
</article>
<div class="research-pair">
<article>
<p class="number">02 / CONTINENTAL SEISMIC IMAGING</p>
<h3>From seismic structure to composition and thermal state</h3>
<p>I combine complementary seismic observations to better constrain crustal
structure and reduce trade-offs among shear-wave velocity, Moho depth, and
Vp/Vs. Current work extends these approaches across the United States to
investigate crustal composition, thermal variations, and possible partial melt
beneath the western U.S.</p>
<a class="text-link" href="research.html#continental">
Continental seismic imaging
</a>
</article>
<article>
<p class="number">03 / INFERENCE &amp; UNCERTAINTY</p>
<h3>How much can we trust a geophysical image?</h3>
<p>
I develop and apply approaches for evaluating what geophysical observations
can reliably resolve, including Bayesian inversion, uncertainty quantification,
and machine-learning methods for seismic data quality control.
</p>
<a class="text-link" href="research.html#computational">
Inference &amp; uncertainty
</a>
</article>
